request: Battery prices since 1991: four claims, true or myth? A two-voice quiz. #interactive #short
subtitle: Four claims about lithium-ion batteries, true or myth? Two hosts argue each one, then the price of an electric car's battery in 1991.
thumb: band "Ten times cheaper? Not even close" stamp "MYTH?"

elements.text: When did batteries get cheap fastest?

spec.title: Battery prices since 1991: true or myth?

sources.title: Battery costs have declined by 99% in the last three decades, making electrified transport a reality
sources.authors: Hannah Ritchie and Pablo Rosado (Our World in Data)
sources.finding: lithium-ion cells cost about $9,200 per kWh in 1991 and $78 in 2024, a fall of more than 99%; cumulative production grew 27 million-fold 1991–2023; the cells in a standard electric car cost around $5,000 today and would have cost over $20,000 a decade earlier

sources.title: Re-examining rates of lithium-ion battery technology improvement and cost decline
sources.authors: M. S. Ziegler and J. E. Trancik
sources.finding: the price of lithium-ion cells fell about 97% from 1991 to 2018

feedback.perfect: You could run a battery factory.
feedback.none: The myths had a full charge today.

commands.speak: How much cheaper have lithium-ion batteries, the ones in our phones and cars, become since 1991? Four claims: true or myth?
First: they're about ten times cheaper than in 1991. Sounds right to me.

quiz.question: Lithium-ion batteries are about ten times cheaper than in 1991. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth: more than a hundred times cheaper, from about nine thousand two hundred dollars per kilowatt-hour in 1991 to seventy-eight in 2024.

commands.speak: Fine. Second: they got cheaper because we made so many of them.

quiz.question: Batteries got cheaper mainly because the world made more of them. True or myth?
quiz.right: True. Production grew twenty-seven million times, and the more the world made, the cheaper each one got.

commands.speak: Then the price must have crashed fastest at the start, in the early nineties.

quiz.question: Battery prices fell fastest in the early 1990s. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth. The early years were slow: the market was tiny, and one company, Sony, held most of the technology.

commands.speak: Last one: the battery cells in an electric car cost about five thousand dollars today.

quiz.question: The battery cells in a standard electric car cost about $5,000 today. True or myth?
quiz.right: True. Only ten years ago, the same cells cost over twenty thousand.

commands.speak: You got {score} of {score_total}. So what would my car's battery have cost in 1991?
Close to six hundred thousand dollars, more than the car itself. That's what a ninety-nine percent fall buys you.
